extracted.intended_audience: media regulators, public-broadcasting policymakers, legal scholars, and public broadcasting professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted standards and obligations governing public service broadcasters (CBC, French national companies, NHK) describing programming mandates, governance, regulatory powers, funding rules, editorial independence and other legal/regulatory requirements. Useful for policy analysis, compliance, and comparative study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predominantly and distinctly Canadian programming
rubrics_metrics.description: “the programming provided by the Corporation should be predominantly and distinctly Canadian” and should reflect Canada and its regions to national and regional audiences while serving the special needs of the regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programming must actually contribute to the flow and exchange of cultural expression across regions; this is a core element of the CBC’s statutory mandate under the Broadcasting Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bilingual programming and linguistic minority needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Programming should be in English and French, reflecting the different needs and circumstances of each official language community, including the particular needs and circumstances of English and French linguistic minorities, and strive to be of equivalent quality in English and French.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates equivalent quality across official languages and coverage of minority-language communities; affects resource allocation and scheduling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribute to shared national consciousness and identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Public broadcasting should contribute to shared national consciousness and identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programming choices should foster national cohesion and identity as part of the public service remit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nationwide availability by appropriate means
rubrics_metrics.description: Programming should be made available throughout Canada by the most appropriate and efficient means and as resources become available for that purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates technical/transmission reach and consideration of resource constraints when planning distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to provide consistent, high-quality information
rubrics_metrics.description: The CBC’s Journalistic Policy Handbook is intended to guarantee that the corporation lives up to its ‘duty to provide consistent, high-quality information upon which all Canadians may rely.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial policies, handbooks and standards are part of meeting this duty; applies to news and current affairs programming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedules driven by public service rather than market imperatives
rubrics_metrics.description: The CBC insists that its schedules be driven by considerations of public service rather than market imperatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programming decisions should prioritise public-service objectives over purely commercial/ratings considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory guarantee of freedom and editorial independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 46(5) of the Broadcasting Act: the Corporation shall enjoy freedom of expression and journalistic, creative and programming independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal protection against political/financial interference; central to CBC’s autonomy and editorial independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board composition and appointment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A Board of Directors of up to twelve members, comprised of prominent citizens from various fields and representing all regions, appointed by the Governor in Council for renewable five-year terms, holding office during good behaviour and removable only for cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Governance design intended to provide regional representation and stability; appointment process is political but removals restricted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Directors’ duties and conflict-of-interest restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Directors owe an obligation of good faith and due diligence to the CBC and its public service mandate, and are not permitted outside activities or dealings in the broadcasting industry which might give rise to conflicts with the CBC’s interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corporate-policy and statutory norms to prevent conflicts and align directors with public-service mandate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal Ombudsman for public complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: CBC retains an internal Ombudsman, fully independent of management, to review serious unresolved public complaints related to the discharge of its mandate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ombudsman reports to the President but lacks statutory binding authority; functions as internal accountability mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parliamentary accountability and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The BA specifies that the CBC shall submit an annual report to Parliament, through the Minister, on its operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal reporting to Parliament provides democratic accountability although CBC retains editorial freedom; Treasury/Parliament also influence funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRTC licensing and standards-setting role
rubrics_metrics.description: The CRTC regulates and supervises aspects of the Canadian broadcasting system, issues, renews and can revoke licences, and may issue guidelines and statements providing guidance to broadcasters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRTC sets overall standards rather than censoring specific programmes; it is an independent agency and must hold public consultations on licence applications and renewals (Section 18).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on Cabinet intervention in CRTC decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Section 28 the Cabinet can override CRTC decisions but only if satisfied the decision derogated from attainment of policy objectives; the Cabinet must refer decisions back to CRTC before final veto and produce reasons for overturning decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cabinet powers are constrained by statutory criteria and requirement to give reasons; this fetters arbitrary political interference and ties actions to Broadcasting Act objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRTC cannot censor specific programmes; sanctions limited
rubrics_metrics.description: The CRTC has no power as a censor of specific CBC programmes but sets overall standards through licensing; licence revocation is the most severe sanction and has never been applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulator’s tools are systemic (licensing, conditions, guidance) rather than content-by-content censorship; enforcement historically cautious.

rubrics_metrics.name: CBC’s procedural protections vis-à-vis CRTC
rubrics_metrics.description: CBC may request consultation if the Commission proposes conditions to CBC licences; no licence issued to the CBC may be suspended or revoked by the CRTC except on application by, or with the consent of, the CBC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory provisions give CBC procedural protections and make renewals largely pro forma while preserving public scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRTC reporting powers when CBC contravenes licence conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Section 25 the CRTC, when satisfied CBC has contravened or failed to comply with any condition, may address a report to the Minister who provides copies to Parliament; Cabinet can issue directions to the CRTC and may direct broadcast of programmes deemed of singular public importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanism for escalating serious compliance issues to political authorities while retaining legal safeguards (e.g., laying orders before Parliament).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public funding and budgetary approval process
rubrics_metrics.description: CBC is primarily financed by public funds, submits a yearly corporate plan and budget to the Minister which may be approved or rejected by the Treasury Board and Parliament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding levels are variable and materially affect the CBC’s ability to fulfil its mandate; public/grant revenue is central (e.g., 66% from federal grant in 1999).

rubrics_metrics.name: CSA must guarantee independence and promote quality/diversity (France)
rubrics_metrics.description: Article premier: the CSA must guarantee the independence and impartiality of public service broadcasting organisations and ensure that all broadcasters promote quality and diversity of programming, national audio-visual production and the French language and culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foundational public service obligations applicable to public and some private broadcasters in France; shapes cahiers des charges and regulatory advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulations on advertising and French/European content (France)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations (approved with Conseil d’Etat and CSA advice) may deal with advertising, broadcasting of programmes of French and European origin during peak hours and contributing to audio-visual production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory/regulatory tools used to promote national/European content and limit commercial influence during key viewing periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of minors in programming (France)
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 15: CSA responsible for ensuring programmes broadcast by either public or private companies do not harm children or adolescents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific statutory duty to safeguard minors; implemented through cahiers des charges and decrees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ban on political advertising (France)
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 14 strictly forbids political advertising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separation of paid political messaging from broadcast advertising; tied to pluralism and election-period rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific public service duties for national programming companies (France)
rubrics_metrics.description: National companies have duties including respect for pluralism, obligations during election campaigns, promotion of orchestras and choirs, educational/social/cultural mission, conservation/exploitation of archives, broadcasting parliamentary debates and messages by political parties/unions/professional bodies, and duty to carry religious programmes on Sunday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cahiers des charges and decrees elaborate these duties and set programme-level obligations consistent with the 1986 Law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cahier des charges as charter of programme obligations (France)
rubrics_metrics.description: A cahier des charges (charter) defines programme obligations of national programming companies and elaborates obligations set out in the 1986 Law; cahiers are fixed by decree on Prime Minister/President’s advice and published in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational instrument that specifies duties such as protecting children, promoting honesty, independence and pluralism in news and political programming, respecting equality and human dignity, and contributing to French language and culture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board composition and representativeness rules (France)
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 47: Boards of Article 44 programming companies have 12 members for a 3-year mandate: one representing each chamber of Parliament, four representing the State, four nominated by the CSA and two representing the workforce; Presidents nominated by the CSA (France 2 and 3 share President) and may be removed by the CSA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed to ensure broad societal representation and to reduce undue political influence over management.

rubrics_metrics.name: CSA powers on election broadcasting, right of reply and political messages (France)
rubrics_metrics.description: The CSA has direct power to establish rules regarding broadcasting during election periods, the right of reply, and broadcasting of messages by political parties, national unions and professional bodies; it is also consulted on advertising rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CSA plays a central role in guaranteeing pluralism and fair access during politically sensitive periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: CSA enforcement and remedies (France)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under amendments (1994) the CSA may order companies to conform to legal obligations, and if not complied with after a warning, suspend a portion of programming for up to one month, impose fines, or order them to broadcast a message that they breached obligations; companies may appeal CSA decisions to the Conseil d’Etat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enhanced enforcement tools give the CSA direct coercive powers short of licence revocation, with judicial review available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licence-fee funding and parliamentary control of distribution (France)
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary funding is the annual licence fee (about 70% of revenues); Parliament sets the rate and approves distribution among programming companies and INA, considering company budgets, production promotion and public service obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial arrangements are politically determined and tied to evaluative criteria related to public-service delivery and production effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict controls on advertising content and quantity (France)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advertising revenues are strictly controlled: overall limits set since 1987; examples include France 2 averages of six minutes/hour and absolute limit of twelve minutes/hour, France 3 five and ten minutes respectively; ads often required to be in French; some product advertising forbidden and interruptions restricted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits justified as safeguarding public order/security and promoting decency, consumer interests and protection of minors; implemented via cahiers des charges and decrees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsorship restrictions (France)
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-news programmes may be sponsored only where they correspond to educational, social and cultural missions; sponsorship must not contain specific promotional references nor encourage purchase; some companies (alcohol, tobacco, prescription drugs) may not sponsor and sponsored programmes must be clearly identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsorship rules protect editorial independence and prevent covert commercial promotion inconsistent with public-service objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broad prohibition on disturbing public security or good morals (Japan)
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 3-2: broadcasters shall not disturb public security, good morals and manners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General statutory constraint on content to protect public order and moral standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political impartiality and accuracy in news (Japan)
rubrics_metrics.description: Broadcasters shall be politically impartial and accurate as regards news and present controversial matters from a variety of viewpoints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory requirement to ensure balanced coverage and plural perspectives, informing editorial standards and complaints handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to provide a variety of programming (Japan)
rubrics_metrics.description: Broadcasters must provide for a variety of programming, including cultural, educational, news and entertainment material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates diverse public-service content mix; NHK’s channel breakdown (e.g., General TV: news, education, culture, entertainment) exemplifies implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility obligations for disabled audiences (Japan)
rubrics_metrics.description: Wherever possible, broadcasters should provide sound messages to help blind persons understand television programmes, and visual images to assist deaf persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages services such as audio description and subtitling/visual assistance to improve accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to establish and publish broadcasting standards (Japan)
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 3-3: broadcasters are required to establish, and make public, broadcasting standards applicable to each type of programming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obligation for transparency of editorial standards and program-specific rules; supports accountability and regulatory review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disaster broadcasting duty to minimise harm (Japan)
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 6-2: in the event of a disaster, broadcasters must conduct programming so as to minimise the harmful effect of the disaster.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes an operational obligation on broadcasters to prioritise public safety and information in emergencies (e.g., rapid news, emergency alerts).
